fragments.text: The Feraferia movement, founded in California in the 1960s, banned technology from its pagan practice.
The salutation 'Thou art God' originates from Robert A. Heinlein's 1961 novel Stranger in a Strange Land and is used by some Witches to acknowledge their own divinity.
Andrew Siliar asserts that the computer revolution and online links are incompatible with the requirements of a Nature Religion.
Isaac Bonewits describes human beings as functioning like radio stations that broadcast and receive wavelengths of magical energy.
The Wiccan ritual circle acts as a liminal threshold that designates a sacred space for the separation and consecration of the practitioner from the mundane world.
Erik Davis introduced the term 'Technopagan' to describe the integration of magic and information technology, challenging the view that the two are mutually exclusive.
